title: Geometric Mode Steering of the Quantum Mpemba Effect
authors: Yingying Hong, Longxing Xu, Weiwei Zhang, Jie Ren, Jianhui Wang
abstract: The slowest Liouvillian mode often bottlenecks the relaxation of an open quantum system to its steady state. Standard strategies circumvent this bottleneck by selecting special initial states or engineering the dissipator. Here we show that neither is necessary. We introduce a pre-dissipative geometric steering protocol that reshapes any given pure or mixed state before relaxation begins -- coherent rotations interleaved with nonselective projective measurements -- at fixed Lindblad generator. By steering the state's Bloch direction along geodesic paths, the protocol suppresses its overlap with the slowest Liouvillian modes. The prepared state then starts farther from equilibrium yet relaxes faster, realizing the quantum Mpemba effect, whenever two computable conditions hold: reduced slow-mode overlap and a larger initial distance to stationarity. Our framework treats real and complex spectral gaps uniformly, and we demonstrate robust Mpemba acceleration in driven qubit and multiqubit systems using operations available in trapped-ion and superconducting platforms.
summary: The paper introduces a novel pre-dissipative geometric mode-steering protocol to accelerate the relaxation of open quantum systems toward equilibrium. By strategically interleaving coherent rotations with nonselective measurements, the protocol suppresses coupling to slow Liouvillian modes. This suppression enables the realization of the quantum Mpemba effect in various qubit platforms.
main_problem: The research addresses how open quantum systems approach their steady state, specifically aiming to realize the quantum Mpemba effect where a state farther from equilibrium relaxes faster.
main_result: A pre-dissipative geometric mode-steering protocol was developed that suppresses overlap with slow Liouvillian modes, enabling accelerated relaxation dynamics in driven qubit and multiqubit systems.
method: The core method involves interleaving coherent unitary evolution segments with nonselective projective measurements to geometrically steer the state's Bloch direction along geodesic paths before dissipation begins.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as an open quantum system governed by a Lindblad master equation, analyzed using generalized Bloch representations for qubit and multiqubit systems. The dynamics are characterized by Liouvillian operators and spectral gaps.
key_observables: Slow-mode Overlap Ratio ($R$), initial distance to stationarity ($\kappa_0$), trace distance $D_T(ho_t, ho_{ss})$, and the final excited-state population $	ilde{p}_e$.
important_parameters: The Mpemba regime requires two conditions: reduced slow-mode overlap ($|R|<1$) and a larger initial distance to stationarity ($\kappa_0 > 1$). The analysis covers both real and complex spectral gaps.
main_assumptions: The protocol is distinct from Zeno protocols as measurements are preparatory. The framework treats real and complex spectral gaps uniformly, though some derivations rely on approximations for the moderately driven regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric steering sequence (Fig. 1a), Bloch trajectories (Fig. 1b), parameter dependence of the Mpemba regime in $(\Omega, \Delta)$ planes (Fig. S2), and time evolution of relaxation dynamics showing slow mode suppression (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem using the Lindblad master equation, details the pre-dissipative geometric steering protocol involving unitary steps and measurements, derives the necessary conditions ($|R|<1$ and $\kappa_0>1$), and demonstrates robust Mpemba acceleration across various qubit architectures.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally implementable quantum control scheme (measurement-based) to overcome fundamental relaxation bottlenecks in open systems, which is highly relevant for quantum computing hardware characterization and optimization.
